thread:
Maya: quick async — planning to flip the quantization profile flag for llamaX from `fp16` -> `int8` in prod. want to define a safe canary + rollback guardrails. suggestions? :thinking:

Jonah: +1 we should do a phased rollout (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated checks after each step. keep initial canary to traffic tagged `beta` and a small random 5% for unseen users.

Rachael: ran offline eval on our reference prompt suite (2k prompts). int8 median accuracy delta = -0.18% vs fp16, worst-case -0.9% on a small category (codegen). overall looks ok but we should protect the codegen flows.

Kai: infra notes — int8 has lower perf variance but slightly higher tail latency on small batches. need to ensure batching config `auto_batch=on` is enabled on the allocation we'll route canary to. otherwise p95 could spike.

Maya: good catch. proposed guardrails:
- auto-rollback if `gen_accuracy_regression_pct` > 0.5% over the canary window
- require p95_latency increase <= 10% AND p50_latency increase <= 5%
- separate rule: if `codegen_error_rate` > 0.2% absolute, block the rollout
- canary window = 30m after traffic shift; manual approval needed to proceed beyond 50%

Jonah: sounds reasonable. confirm metric names for the deploy pipeline so the deploy bot can watch them: `model.gen_accuracy_regression_pct`, `http.p50_latency_ms`, `http.p95_latency_ms`, `model.codegen_error_rate`.

Rachael: I can add a targeted prompt set for codegen and wire it into the QA checks (will push to `ci/evals/int8-rollout`). expect results in ~90m.

Kai: infra will create a dedicated nodepool `llamaX-int8-canary` with reserved capacity and `auto_batch=on`. also enabling prefix KV cache bypass for canary to avoid cache warmup noise.

Maya: feature flag name: `ff.quant.profile.llamaX`. values: `fp16`, `int8`, `int4`. rollout command (internal):
```
# rollout 5% to beta + 5% random
flagctl rollout --flag ff.quant.profile.llamaX --to 5% --audience tag:beta --variant int8
flagctl rollout --flag ff.quant.profile.llamaX --to 5% --audience random --variant int8
```

Jonah: add these automated checks to the deploy job:
- wait 30m, sample 2k requests from canary, compute metrics
- compare to baseline snapshot (previous 24h rolling)
- if any guardrail fails -> run `flagctl rollback --flag ff.quant.profile.llamaX --variant fp16`

deploy-bot: noted. will watch metrics and post pass/fail in thread. link to dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/d/quant-rollouts?var-model=llamaX

Rachael: eval finished early: codegen subset regression = 0.62% (slightly above 0.5). full suite regression = 0.19%. so codegen is the only problem area.

Maya: ok based on that we should exclude `tag:codegen` from initial canary audiences and route them to fp16 for now. we can try targeted mitigations (quant-aware calibration) before flipping codegen.

Jonah: agree. new rollout plan:
- 5% beta + 5% random, excluding `tag:codegen`
- monitor the listed metrics for 30m; autopause/rollback thresholds as discussed
- if stable, 25% (same exclusion), then run a targeted canary for `tag:codegen` in a dedicated nodepool with quant-calibrated weights

Kai: I'll prep the nodepool and the feature flag audience exclusion rule: `audience != tag:codegen`. also adding a temporary rate limit on canary nodes at 200rps to avoid stress.

Maya: action items:
- Rachael: checkin PR with codegen eval dataset + threshold config -> `#pr`
- Jonah: update deploy pipeline to run the guardrail checks and automatic rollback -> `#pr`
- Kai: create nodepool and set batching/cache config -> `#infra-ticket`

Rachael: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/evals/pull/412. local numbers and config in the diff. :eyes:

Jonah: PR for pipeline changes in draft, pinging Eng-Oncall for a quick review before enabling autopilot.

deploy-bot: starting 5% canary (beta + random, excluding tag:codegen). will post results in 30m. :robot_face:

Maya: thanks all — post results here and we’ll decide next step. :thumbsup:
